summary: I sent the exact brief, with no visual cues. The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, read the settings files, and read the visual-companion guide. It then started scripts/start-server.sh and wrote one HTML screen with three candidate layouts (A: stacked sections, B: sidebar, C: tabs). It gave me a localhost URL with a key and asked me to pick a layout and confirm the groups. I picked A. It then changed settings.html and settings.css and added a .gitignore. It wrote no spec and no plan.
reasoning: All eight criteria are met, based on the session log, the screen and git status. The agent decided on its own that a layout question was worth a visual. It opened the companion only once it had a concrete layout question to show. It kept the design in chat, wrote no spec or plan documents, and waited for my pick before changing any code.

observations.description: First-run Claude Code dialogs (workspace trust and Bypass Permissions warning) put the cursor on 'No, exit' by default, so I had to press Down before Enter on each. This is a harness/environment issue, not part of the SUT.
The agent says "I've opened three layout sketches in a browser tab", but it only started a server and printed a URL. Nothing was opened automatically, so the wording could mislead the user.
The agent added the note "Sketching uses a lot of tokens, so tell me if you'd rather stay in the terminal." A user might not care about that cost, but the opt-out is reasonable.

When the companion server shut down, the terminal filled with long red 'Deleted .hyperpowers/brainstorm/.../state/server.log' diff blocks showing full JSON paths and keys. This is noisy and pushes the summary off screen.
The agent edited settings.html with an inline python3 heredoc through Bash instead of the Edit tool. It worked, but it's harder to review in the transcript.
The agent proposed adding a .gitignore for .hyperpowers/ and asked first, which is good. It is still a scope addition beyond the layout task.

The agent says it did not check the new styling in a browser ("hasn't been checked visually"). It was honest about this, but it never showed the final page in the companion before shutting the server down.

criteria.evidence: Session log bd3fc937…jsonl: the first tool call is {"n":"Skill","i":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:brainstorming\"}"}, before any edits. It is the only Skill call in the log.

criteria.criterion: Visual companion opened: start-server.sh run, localhost URL given, HTML screen written
criteria.evidence: Log shows a Bash call to …/skills/brainstorming/scripts/start-server.sh --project-dir …, then a Write to .hyperpowers/brainstorm/28839-1790841278/content/layout.html containing 'A: Stacked sections' mockups. Screen: "I've opened three layout sketches in a browser tab: http://localhost:54279/?key=a896a7b7…"

criteria.criterion: Opened just-in-time, not upfront; no non-visual questions routed through the browser
criteria.evidence: Log order: Skill → git ls-files → cat settings files → read visual-companion.md → start-server.sh → write layout.html → message. Nothing announced the companion before the layout question came up. The agent asked no separate non-visual questions, and its group-confirmation question was asked in the terminal ("please also answer here").

criteria.criterion: Bounded classification held; no ceremony escalation
criteria.evidence: The design stayed in chat: one message listed the four groups and options A, B and C with a recommendation. After my pick, the agent went straight to implementation ("Implementing: each group becomes a <fieldset>…"). No spec, plan or other extra steps.

`ls docs` in the workdir returned 'No such file or directory'. `git status --short` shows only 'M public/settings.css', 'M public/settings.html', '?? .gitignore'. `find . -name '*.md'` found only ./README.md.

criteria.criterion: No plan document / writing-plans not invoked
criteria.evidence: jq over the log for Skill tool_use inputs returns only 'hyperpowers:brainstorming'. grep for 'writing-plans' matched only the list of available skills. No plan .md files on disk.

criteria.criterion: Asked for approval of layout before implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Which layout do you want, and do those four groups look right? You can click an option in the browser, but please also answer here." The first edit to settings.html came only after my reply.

Log after my reply: "Implementing: each group becomes a `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>` heading…", followed by edits to public/settings.html and settings.css. Final screen: "The settings page now uses the stacked layout you picked, in four headed sections…"
